kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: unbranded/generic, packaged and sold by ELEGOO as part of this kit
identity.manufacturer_part_number: not applicable, generic wire with no manufacturer part number
generic_equivalents: any 2.54 mm pitch Dupont-style male-to-female jumper wire
identity.package: single-conductor wire, female socket housing on one end and a bare male pin on the other

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A single wire with a socket on one end and a plug on the other, used to connect a sensor module's pin to a breadboard or an Arduino pin without soldering.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Connecting a module that has header pins sticking up, such as the IR receiver or the DHT11 humidity sensor, to a breadboard hole or directly to an Arduino UNO pin.
function.how_it_works_briefly: One end is a small metal socket inside a plastic housing that slides over a pin. The other end is a bare metal pin that pushes straight into a breadboard hole. It is just a wire, it does not change or process the signal passing through it.

pinout.name: single conductor
pinout.role: carries whatever signal, power, or ground line it is wired to, it has no fixed role of its own
pinout.notes: one end terminates in a female socket housing, the other end is a bare male pin

pins.pin_1_identification: This part carries only one wire, so there is no 'pin 1'. Instead, look for the two different ends: the female end has a small rectangular plastic housing with a hole in the tip, made to slide over a pin. The male end is a bare metal pin sticking out of a smaller housing, made to push into a breadboard hole or a female housing.

electrical.operating_voltage: not specified by ELEGOO for this exact wire, well below the connector's rated voltage in this kit's 5-12V circuits
electrical.absolute_max_voltage: 250V, generic rating for a Dupont-style 2.54 mm connector, not a measurement of this exact wire
electrical.typical_current: well under 1A, this kit only uses it for signal-level connections
electrical.max_current: up to about 3A per contact, generic rating for a Dupont-style 2.54 mm connector using 22-28 AWG wire
electrical.logic_level: not applicable, it is a plain wire with no electronics inside

key_specs.note: these are generic specs for this class of Dupont-style connector and wire, not measurements from an ELEGOO datasheet for this exact wire (see confidence.notes)

visual_identification.shape_and_size: A single thin, flexible wire roughly 20 cm (about 8 inches) long. One end has a small rectangular black plastic housing about 6-8 mm long with a socket hole in the tip. The other end has a similar small housing but with a bare metal pin, about 3 mm long, sticking straight out.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Usually sold in an assortment of solid colors (red, black, yellow, blue, green, etc). No printed text or markings on the wire or housings.
easily_confused_with: breadboard jumper wire (jumper-wire, solid pins on both ends, no socket)
male-to-male Dupont wire (bare pin on both ends)
female-to-female Dupont wire (socket housing on both ends)

example_connections.uno_pin: plugs onto a module's header pin (for example, the DHT11 sensor's data pin) or directly onto an Arduino UNO digital or analog pin
pushes into any breadboard hole in the row you want to connect

required_extra_parts: a breadboard, or a module/board with header pins to plug into
wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: none, it is a passive wire

hazards: none at the low voltages used in this kit (5-12V)
could short two circuit nodes together if both bare ends touch the same exposed metal at once
handling_notes: pull on the plastic housing, not the wire itself, when unplugging it
avoid bending the same spot repeatedly, the thin strand inside can fatigue and break invisibly under the insulation
common_mistakes: plugging the male end into the wrong header pin, always check which signal you are connecting before powering on
assuming a broken connection is a code bug when it is actually a bent or broken pin inside the wire

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: sensor or module does not respond at all
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: the wire looks connected but the strand inside is broken, common after repeated bending
symptoms_and_causes.check: gently wiggle the wire while the circuit is running and watch for the connection to cut in and out, or swap in a different wire

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: a worn-out female socket that no longer grips the pin tightly
symptoms_and_causes.check: try to wiggle the connector where it sits on the pin, if it moves easily the socket has worn out

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: Set the multimeter to continuity or resistance mode. Touch one probe to the metal at the male end and the other probe inside the opening of the female socket. A working wire beeps or reads near 0 ohms. A broken wire reads infinite resistance (often shown as 'OL' or '1').

typical_suppliers: generic electronics retailers such as Amazon and eBay sell female-to-male Dupont wire packs separately
